subject: physics
stem: Consider a current carrying wire (current $I$) in the shape of a circle. Note that as the current progresses along the wire, the direction of $\mathbf{j}$ (current density) changes in an exact manner, while the current $I$ remain unaffected. The agent that is essentially responsible for is
options: source of emf.
electric field produced by charges accumulated on the surface of wire.
the charges just behind a given segment of wire which push them just the right way by repulsion.
the charges ahead.

checks.notes: Transcription matches page; surface charges set up the field steering current, key B agrees.

subject: physics
stem: Two batteries of emf $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$ ($\varepsilon_2 > \varepsilon_1$) and internal resistances $r_1$ and $r_2$ respectively are connected in parallel as shown in Fig 3.1.
options: The equivalent emf $\varepsilon_{eq}$ of the two cells is between $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$, i.e. $\varepsilon_1 < \varepsilon_{eq} < \varepsilon_2$.
The equivalent emf $\varepsilon_{eq}$ is smaller than $\varepsilon_1$.
The $\varepsilon_{eq}$ is given by $\varepsilon_{eq} = \varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2$ always.
$\varepsilon_{eq}$ is independent of internal resistances $r_1$ and $r_2$.

subject: physics
stem: A resistance $R$ is to be measured using a meter bridge. Student chooses the standard resistance $S$ to be $100\,\Omega$. He finds the null point at $l_1 = 2.9\,\mathrm{cm}$. He is told to attempt to improve the accuracy. Which of the following is a useful way?
options: He should measure $l_1$ more accurately.
He should change $S$ to $1000\,\Omega$ and repeat the experiment.
He should change $S$ to $3\,\Omega$ and repeat the experiment.
He should give up hope of a more accurate measurement with a meter bridge.

subject: physics
stem: Two cells of emf's approximately $5\,\mathrm{V}$ and $10\,\mathrm{V}$ are to be accurately compared using a potentiometer of length $400\,\mathrm{cm}$.
options: The battery that runs the potentiometer should have voltage of $8\,\mathrm{V}$.
The battery of potentiometer can have a voltage of $15\,\mathrm{V}$ and $R$ adjusted so that the potential drop across the wire slightly exceeds $10\,\mathrm{V}$.
The first portion of $50\,\mathrm{cm}$ of wire itself should have a potential drop of $10\,\mathrm{V}$.
Potentiometer is usually used for comparing resistances and not voltages.

subject: physics
stem: A metal rod of length $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ and a rectangular cross-section of $1\,\mathrm{cm}\times\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{cm}$ is connected to a battery across opposite faces. The resistance will be
options: maximum when the battery is connected across $1\,\mathrm{cm}\times\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{cm}$ faces.
maximum when the battery is connected across $10\,\mathrm{cm}\times 1\,\mathrm{cm}$ faces.
maximum when the battery is connected across $10\,\mathrm{cm}\times\frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{cm}$ faces.
same irrespective of the three faces.

subject: physics
stem: Which of the following characteristics of electrons determines the current in a conductor?
options: Drift velocity alone.
Thermal velocity alone.
Both drift velocity and thermal velocity.
Neither drift nor thermal velocity.
